mappings.note: Whom the sangatkaar reminds of his childhood (the pramukh gaayak) - identification. LO-7 rejected: the reminder is stated in the poem, nothing is being interpreted.
Gloss of 'sthaayi' as the geet's main tek. LO-2 rejected: sthaayi belongs to the song described in the poem, not to this kavita's own tuk, lay, yati or gati.
Meaning of 'anhad' in the poem's context - a comprehension gloss of the text's vocabulary. C-H1.2 rejected: no grammar operation (sandhi, samaas, vilom) is performed.
What 'taarsaptak' names (sargam's high register) - vocabulary gloss inside the poem. LO-2 rejected: it is a music term in the content, not a formal upaadaan of the kavita.
WHEN he gives dhaandhas (as the raag begins to fall) - the circumstance the poem states. LO-7 rejected: the item asks the occasion, not what the consoling signifies.
Why the main singer's voice fails (gala baith jaana) - a factual detail about the main singer. LO-7 rejected: the cause is in the lines, no bhaav reading is needed.
Who makes him feel he is not alone - identification. LO-7 rejected: only the agent is asked.
His main role, answered by the poem's own statement (giving the voice strength). LO-7 rejected: the items asking what that role stands for in society are the LO-7 ones.
Whose job it is to add a goonj to the garajdaar voice - identification (a duplicate stem, same mapping as its twin in file 1). LO-7 rejected: only the agent is asked.
Whose voice is called beautiful, weak and trembling - identification. LO-7 rejected: the interpretive 'why is it called that' item is mapped LO-7 instead.
Who is reminded of childhood after losing the swar (the gaayak) - content recall. LO-7 rejected: the poem states the episode outright.
WHO never lifts his voice above the main singer's - identification. LO-7 rejected: the 'why he does not' item is the interpretive one and takes LO-7.
Attribution of the poem to Manglesh Dabral is literary knowledge, not reading of the text. LO-6 rejected: nothing in the poem answers it.
Which art the poem's accompanists belong to (gaayan) - content recall. LO-7 rejected: the item that extends the sangatkaar to other fields is the thematic one and takes LO-7.
Gloss of 'antara' (the geet's charan other than the tek). LO-2 rejected: a term of the song inside the poem, not an upaadaan of this kavita.

Synonym for 'dhaadhas baandhna', a phrase the poem itself uses - a meaning gloss of the text. C-H1.2 rejected: that competency is for grammar items with no poem content, and this one is the poem's own idiom.
Meaning of 'jatil' as the poem uses it (jatil taanon mein). C-H1.2 rejected: no grammar operation is performed, it is a comprehension gloss.
Meaning of 'nausikhiya', the poem's own word for the main singer's early days. C-H1.2 rejected: a gloss inside the text, not a vyaakaran exercise.
Asks the reader to establish the tyaag in the sangatkaar - an appraisal of the poem's bhaav-paksh. LO-6 rejected: no line states this, it must be argued from the poem.
Why a hichak seems to be in his voice - the same bhaav-paksh reading as the MCQ twins in file 1. LO-6 rejected: the reason is interpretive, not narrated.

WHEN the sangatkaar's role becomes visible - the answer is the poem's stated occasions (the voice breaking, straying in anhad). LO-7 rejected: the occasions are in the text; the item on what his role means to society is mapped LO-7.
What kind of person the sangatkaar is a PRATIK of - symbol reading, the poem's core bhaav. LO-6 rejected: the answer lies outside the literal narrative.
In which roles the sangatkaar helps the main singers - an enumeration of the poem's content. LO-7 rejected: the acts are listed in the text, no symbolic reading required.
The utility of sangatkaar-like people in life generally - extends the poem's pratik beyond the text. LO-6 rejected: this is the poem's message, not its narrated content.
How the poet brings out the sangatkaar's manushyata - explicitly bhaav-paksh explication. LO-6 rejected: it asks how the poet achieves it, not what happens.
WHY his voice is called weak and trembling - reads the poet's intent behind the description. LO-6 rejected: the identification version of this item is the one mapped LO-6.
Which sort of people the poet points to through the sangatkaar - pratik reading. LO-6 rejected: the answer is outside the literal music scene.
What kind of person the sangatkaar symbolises - the poem's pratik, so bhaav-paksh. LO-6 rejected: not recoverable as a stated fact.
The relation between main singer and sangatkaar since ancient times - content the poem states. LO-7 rejected: the item reports the relation rather than interpreting it.
Who is called great in the poem AND why - an evaluative reading of the poet's sympathy. LO-6 rejected: the 'why' half cannot be answered from a single line.
Generalises the poem to anyone faltering near the peak of success and the colleagues who steady him - the pratik applied beyond the text. LO-6 rejected: the stem leaves the poem's literal scene.
His role and HOW he keeps the voice from scattering - the mechanism the poem describes. LO-7 rejected: the answer narrates what he does, not what it signifies.
When the singer's prerna deserts him and what he then feels - factual detail about the main singer. LO-7 rejected: the lines state both.
In which roles sangatkaars help the main singers - enumeration of the poem's content (duplicate stem, mapped as its twin). LO-7 rejected: no symbolic reading is asked.
Where sangatkaar-like people appear outside music - carries the poem's pratik into other fields. LO-6 rejected: the answer is not in the poem's literal content.
WHY he never lifts his voice above the main singer's - the manushyata reading at the heart of the poem. LO-6 rejected: the 'who does not' version is the factual one and is mapped LO-6.
Why able people like the sangatkaar stay in the back row of society - the poem's social message, five-mark bhaav-paksh. LO-6 rejected: it argues from the poem rather than reporting it.
How he supports the singer and brings him back to his nausikhiya state - the poem's narrated content. LO-7 rejected: the expected answer retells the lines rather than weighing their bhaav.
